steps.context: Input files: /eval-sonnet-r2-without-paired-n5-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 11 columns: gene symbol + 10 samples) and /eval-sonnet-r2-without-paired-n5-2/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (10 rows: subject, condition, and sample id columns). Design is fully paired: 5 subjects x 2 conditions (control, treated), raw integer counts from STAR/featureCounts.
steps.question: Within the 5 paired subjects, which genes are differentially expressed between the treated and control blood samples when subject identity is modeled as a blocking factor?
constraints: Use a paired/blocked model (subject + condition), not an unpaired two-sample test — the design is paired and ignoring subject as a blocking factor will misstate significance
Filter genes with near-zero counts across all samples before fitting to avoid unstable dispersion estimates given the modest 12000-gene, 10-sample matrix
Verify metadata sample identifiers match the counts column headers exactly before merging; do not assume ordering
acceptance_criteria: Counts (12000 genes x 10 samples) and metadata (10 rows: subject, condition, plus sample id) are loaded and joined correctly by sample identifier
Design model includes subject as a covariate/blocking term and condition (control vs treated) as the factor of interest (paired design, e.g. ~ subject + condition in DESeq2)
Low-count genes are filtered before dispersion estimation
Output includes a full results table with log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (padj) per gene, ranked by significance
A summary reports the number of genes at padj < 0.05 and the number at a more permissive padj < 0.1, plus direction (up/down in treated)
QC diagnostics reported: library size per sample, PCA or sample-distance clustering to confirm subject pairing dominates a plausible axis and treatment separates samples

steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes that respond to treatment within subjects (from the paired DE analysis)?
constraints: Match gene identifiers exactly to HGNC symbols as used in counts.csv; do not assume Ensembl IDs are present
Parse the WikiPathways GMT by splitting the '%'-delimited first field to recover a readable pathway name and WikiPathways ID before reporting results
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment is run on the full ranked/annotated gene list from T1S1 (not just an arbitrary top-N cut), using either a significance-threshold gene-set overrepresentation test or a rank-based (GSEA-style) test
Pathway gene sets are the WikiPathways Homo sapiens collection available in this environment, matched on HGNC gene symbols consistent with the counts.csv gene identifiers
Output reports enriched pathway name, WikiPathways ID, gene overlap/leading-edge genes, and BH-adjusted p-value
If zero pathways pass FDR < 0.25 (plausible given the small 5-pair cohort and 12000-gene background), the step reports this explicitly rather than lowering thresholds silently

plan.title: Paired control-vs-treated DE analysis, 5 subjects
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a paired bulk RNA-seq design: 5 subjects, each contributing a control and a treated blood sample (12000 genes x 10 samples, raw STAR/featureCounts integer counts). The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — calls for a paired differential expression model that accounts for subject-to-subject variability (a paired/blocked design) rather than an unpaired two-group test, since biological variation between subjects would otherwise inflate residual variance and mask consistent treatment effects. Step 1 performs QC and paired DESeq2 (or edgeR paired design) analysis with subject as a blocking factor and condition (control vs treated) as the factor of interest, producing a single genome-wide DE gene list for the treatment effect controlled for subject identity. Step 2 takes that ranked gene list and performs pathway enrichment against WikiPathways Homo sapiens gene sets, present in this environment, to characterize the biological programs perturbed by treatment. This two-step flow directly answers the stated research question (paired within-subject treatment response) and adds mechanistic context without overreaching into any translational/clinical scope not requested.
